title: A writing task leaves nothing to guess
statement: A writing task must say what to write about, in what form, at what length and from which sources, leaving the student nothing to guess.
example: One rubric requires four things of every extended-writing prompt: the topic, the form, the length and the sources.
detail: The evaluator's extended-writing rubric requires every prompt to specify what to write about, the form, how long or how many paragraphs, and what sources to use (`shadow/bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/ecr_evaluation.txt` lines 119-120). A mandatory audit fails the prompt outright when the writing mode is unclear or a student can't tell the genre from the prompt alone (lines 54-60). The short-answer rubric likewise requires the stem to say exactly what the student needs to write about, and fails vague stems and stems that ask two questions (`question/scr_evaluation.txt` lines 124-129).

evidence.quote: - The prompt must specify: (a) what to write about, (b) what form to write in, (c) how long/how many paragraphs are expected, (d) what sources to use.
A student must be able to determine what kind of writing is expected without guessing.
- The question stem must specify exactly what the student needs to write about.
